statement: If the decreasing finite-stage complement densities tend to zero, the infinite complement has logarithmic density zero. Consequently the full problem holds whenever the moduli are pairwise coprime: CRT gives a product density, with the divergent reciprocal branch handled by the zero-limit lemma and the convergent branch by a uniform tail union bound.
dependency_gaps: The general case with a positive finite-stage density limit remains.
Conditional new-class asymptotic densities do not yet control their lcm-scale onset transients.
No higher-order CRT overlap inequality closes the dependent case.
